description:
The surah that opens with the oath of the Divine One swearing by **The Sun** as it shines out with morning's radiance. It is named after "the sun" (al-shams), mentioned in verse 1. The central theme of the surah touch upon purifying or corrupting the soul, with the tribe of Thamūd given as an example of corruption.
The surah is also known as Sol

14.1: Or 'destroyed them,' or 'crushed them,' or 'brought down His punishment (or wrath) upon them.'
14.2: That is, razed their city to the ground.

translations.1: By the sun and her forenoon splendour,
translations.2: by the moon when he follows her,
translations.3: by the day when it reveals her,
translations.4: by the night when it covers her,
translations.5: by the sky and Him who built it,
translations.6: by the earth and Him who spread it,
translations.7: by the soul and Him who fashioned it,
translations.8:
and inspired it with
   [discernment between] its virtues and vices:
translations.9: one who purifies it is felicitous,
translations.10: and one who betrays it fails.
translations.11:
The [people of] Thamūd denied [Allah's signs]
   out of their rebellion,
translations.12: when the most wretched of them rose up.
translations.13:
But then the apostle of Allah said to them,
  'Let Allah's she-camel drink!'
translations.14:
But they impugned him and then hamstrung her,
  so their Lord took them unawares by night<{["F", 1]}>
   because of their sin,
  and levelled it.<{["F", 2]}>
translations.15: And He does not fear its outcome.
